title: Modi Lands in Nice and Heads to Bratislava. No Indian PM Has Ever Visited Slovakia.
excerpt: The six-day European tour includes the first-ever prime ministerial visit to the Slovak Republic, a bilateral with Macron, and a G7 seat at Evian where he may face Trump for the first time since the tariff war.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi touched down in Nice on Saturday, beginning a six-day swing through France and Slovakia that will culminate in his seventh consecutive appearance at the G7 Summit — and his first face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump since the tariff war cratered bilateral ties last year.

But the most symbolically loaded stop comes first. On June 14, Modi will arrive in Bratislava for a three-day state visit to the Slovak Republic — the first by any Indian prime minister since Slovakia became an independent nation in 1993.

## A Blank Page, Already Being Filled

The visit is not merely ceremonial. India-Slovakia bilateral trade has doubled in just three years, jumping from €800 million in 2023 to €1.6 billion in 2025 — one of the sharpest trade accelerations India has achieved with any European nation in recent memory.

Slovak Ambassador Robert Maxian called the visit "historic, strategic, and symbolic," noting that the prime ministers of both countries have never met in person before. He described the recently concluded India-EU Free Trade Agreement as the "mother of deals," predicting it would double trade figures further.

At Bratislava Castle on June 15, Modi will hold delegation-level talks with Slovak PM Robert Fico and meet President Peter Pellegrini. The two sides are expected to sign agreements covering automobile manufacturing, railway infrastructure, renewable energy, cybersecurity, and defense production. A state banquet at the Presidential Palace will follow.

## Nice and Evian: The Macron Bilateral and the G7 Table

The Slovakia detour sits inside a larger diplomatic arc. In Nice, Modi will hold a bilateral with French President Emmanuel Macron on June 14 — their first since the India-France relationship was elevated to a "Special Global Strategic Partnership" in February. The two leaders will jointly inaugurate "Bharat Innovates," a showcase of 120 Indian deep-tech startups alongside French and international venture capital, held during the India-France Year of Innovation.

From June 16 to 17, Modi moves to Evian-les-Bains for the 52nd G7 Summit, where France has invited India as a partner country. This marks India's 13th G7 participation and Modi's seventh in a row — a frequency that underscores the group's recognition of India's weight in global governance.

## The Trump Question

The most watched moment may be a bilateral that has not been officially confirmed. Reuters, citing an Indian government source, reported that Modi is "likely" to hold talks with Trump on the sidelines, with trade tariffs, H-1B visas, energy cooperation, and the Iran war on the table.

The meeting would be their first since the trade breakdown of mid-2025, when U.S. tariffs on Indian goods climbed to 50 percent and Trump's repeated claims of mediating the India-Pakistan conflict soured relations. Recent high-level engagement — including Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India last month — has thawed some of the ice, and a first tranche of a bilateral trade deal could be finalized by mid-July, according to India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal.

For the five million Indian Americans navigating work visas, green card backlogs, and tariff uncertainty, the G7 sidelines may carry more practical consequence than the summit itself.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

Modi's European tour is not just about summits and signatures. The Slovakia visit signals India's push to diversify its European partnerships beyond the traditional anchors of London, Berlin, and Paris. For NRIs in continental Europe, deeper India-Slovakia ties in automotive, rail, and energy could open new business and professional corridors.

And at Evian, the India-U.S. conversation — if it happens — will touch the nerves that matter most: the future of H-1B policy, the trajectory of trade tariffs, and whether the two largest democracies can rebuild a working relationship after a bruising year.

Modi's plane has landed. The harder landings are still ahead.
